title: Gas prices this week: why they are high and how to spend less
dek: AAA's national average hit $4.48 on September 24, a record for this time of year. Here are proven ways to get more miles from each gallon.
keyPoints: AAA's national average for regular was $4.48 on September 24, up nearly 5 cents in a week.
Brent crude traded around $104.46 a barrel late Monday morning, up about 1.7 percent from Friday.
Aggressive driving can cut highway mileage by roughly 15% to 30%, per FuelEconomy.gov.
Each 5 mph over 50 mph is like paying about $0.21 more per gallon.

Gas Mileage Tips - Driving More Efficiently

body: If the pump looked expensive on your way to work, the numbers back that up. AAA put the national average for a gallon of regular at $4.48 on September 24, up nearly 5 cents from the week before and the highest average it has recorded for this time of year. Earlier in the month, AAA pointed to crude oil near $100 a barrel and tension around the Strait of Hormuz.

Oil kept climbing into this week. Fortune reported Brent crude at about $104.46 a barrel late Monday morning, up about 1.7 percent from the previous business day and more than 15 percent over the past month. Pump prices usually follow crude with a lag, so it is hard to say exactly where they will go next.

The part you can control is how far each gallon goes. The U.S. Department of Energy's FuelEconomy.gov says speeding, rapid acceleration and hard braking can lower gas mileage by roughly 15 to 30 percent at highway speeds and 10 to 40 percent in stop-and-go traffic. It also estimates that each 5 mph you drive over 50 mph is like paying about 21 cents more per gallon, and that idling can burn a quarter to a half gallon an hour.

A few other habits help. Combining errands into one trip cuts miles, cruise control on the highway usually saves gas, and a price app or AAA's state averages page can show whether the station on your route is higher than others nearby. For bigger budget questions, a nonprofit credit counselor or your local consumer agency can help with your own situation.
On this morning's drive, try easing off the gas when you accelerate and keeping your highway speed a few miles per hour lower. It costs nothing, and it adds up over a week of commuting.
